solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Retired city keyboard player, not a mountaineer

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the city's name is read from the end
'not a' tells us one letter A is to be dropped from the musician's title

blocks.note: LA is short for Los Angeles
the letter taken out of the player

explanation.surface: A retired pianist from some city is apparently not a climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a mountaineer' reads as a denial, but 'not a' is the deletion and 'mountaineer' alone is the definition: AL + PI(A)NIST gives ALPINIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpinist is a climber of high peaks, the Alps lending the name to the whole sport.

clue.text: Knock Indian city briefly in burlesque

indicators.note: said briefly, the city's name is cut short by its final letter

blocks.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
Poona is the older spelling of Pune

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an Indian city in a comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Poona, the old name of Pune, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a mocking parody that ridicules its subject through comic exaggeration.

clue.text: Asian working in co-ed: he's popular to begin with

indicators.note: letters set working are put into action in a fresh arrangement
this phrase puts the word for popular at the front of the rest

explanation.surface: An Asian student at a mixed school is the popular one from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of the surface belongs to the anagram fodder, while a second IN comes from 'popular'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indochinese describes a person from the Southeast Asian peninsula of Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia.

clue.text: Current authority protecting large part of Scotland

indicators.note: one word protecting another wraps around it on both sides

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
to have the say is to have authority
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A water authority looks after a big stretch of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: I + SA(L)Y. Islay is an island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is a Hebridean island off Scotland's west coast, so it is a region of that country.

clue.text: Quake when young chorister crosses minister at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the clergyman's word
the singer crosses over, straddling the other letter so it sits inside

blocks.note: a boy soprano in a choir

explanation.surface: A choirboy shakes as he walks past the minister in church.
explanation.walkthrough: TRE(M)BLE: a treble is a boy who sings the top part in a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble is to shake or shudder, as a quake does.

clue.text: Scandinavian pirate's female leader

explanation.surface: A Norse raider's band is led by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of pirate's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikings were seafaring Norse raiders who plundered the coasts of Europe.

clue.text: One watching Roman poet leaving right before

indicators.note: a letter leaving the poet's name is taken out of it

explanation.surface: Someone observes a Roman poet who went off to the right earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: VIRGIL without R gives VIGIL, followed by ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante is a self-appointed guardian who keeps watch over a neighbourhood outside the law.

clue.text: Parrot Eliot initially pinched from another poet

indicators.note: something pinched from a word is stolen away, so it is removed

blocks.note: the poet T S Eliot's initials

explanation.surface: A parrot was stolen by Eliot from another poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like it wants Eliot's first letter, but it means his initials, T S, which come off KEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: The kea is a large olive-green parrot native to New Zealand's mountains.

clue.text: Dropping off, like some acquaintances?

blocks.note: second meaning: describing people one knows only well enough to greet

explanation.walkthrough: A nodding acquaintance is someone you know only slightly, enough to nod to in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means drowsing with a drooping head, and also describes a slight acquaintance marked by a mere nod.

clue.text: Legal-minded don loses nothing cracking up the shires

indicators.note: the don's phrase loses a letter, which is taken out before rearranging
something cracking up breaks into pieces that can be reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A legally minded university teacher has a breakdown in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: Middle England is the conservative middle-class heartland of English provincial towns and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The shires are the rural English counties, standing for the conventional provincial heartland called Middle England.

clue.text: Petulant model ringing a London hospital

indicators.note: to ring something is to circle it, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: a toy is a model, as in a toy car

explanation.surface: A sulky fashion model telephones a London hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: TO(UCH)Y; 'ringing' suggests a phone call but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone touchy takes offence easily, which is close to being sulky or petulant.

clue.text: Shot during news broadcast

blocks.note: a shot fired from a gun
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: A shooting happens while the news is on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news report broadcast on radio or television.

clue.text: Undying Latin verse recollecting gods primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the deities is used
re-collecting means gathering up again, so the letters are reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Immortal Latin poetry recalls the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Everlasting means lasting forever, which is what undying means.

clue.text: Aussie possibly opposed to work, backing head of faculty

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for work is read in reverse

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a dean heads a university faculty

explanation.surface: An Australian might be against working, supporting the dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like supporting the dean but reverses OP; 'possibly' marks an Aussie as only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes are Australia and New Zealand, so an Australian is one example of an Antipodean.

clue.text: Attack cricket side's mirth without hesitation

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so the hesitation sound is dropped

blocks.note: the on side in cricket, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A cricket team is attacked for laughing without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side is the half of a cricket field on the batter's leg side; LAUGHTER loses ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, sustained attack or assault.

clue.text: Brittle BBC boss welcomed by the old in retirement

indicators.note: something in retirement has withdrawn or gone back, so the archaic word is read backwards
a guest welcomed by a host is taken inside

blocks.note: ye is the old form of the
the BBC is headed by the Director-General

explanation.surface: A nervy BBC chief is welcomed by pensioners after he retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old' looks like elderly people, but it is the archaic form of 'the'; 'in retirement' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and easily snapped, so a brittle temper fits it.

clue.text: With which a fencer may score record points?

definitions.text: With which a fencer may score

blocks.note: two compass points, east and east

explanation.surface: A question of which weapon a fencer scores hits with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record points' sounds like tallying points scored, but each word gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The épée is one of the three fencing swords, and a touch with it scores.

clue.text: Old hairpiece found in cable over in Tamworth?

indicators.note: turned over, the word for cable runs the other way
in places the flipped cable inside the animal

blocks.note: the Tamworth is a breed of pig; the question mark flags an example

explanation.surface: An old wig found tangled in a cable in the town of Tamworth.
explanation.walkthrough: WIRE reversed is ERIW, placed in PIG. Tamworth looks like the English town, but it is a ginger breed of pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A periwig is the long powdered wig worn in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

clue.text: Eg Man Ray in county mostly associated with top people

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the county loses its last letter

blocks.note: Surrey is an English county south of London
the A-list, the most celebrated people

explanation.surface: Man Ray mixed with the elite in an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Man Ray, the American photographer and artist, was a leading figure of the Surrealist movement.

clue.text: Went round gallery, visiting bar

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the gallery sits within the bar

blocks.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone toured a gallery after dropping into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: RO(TATE)D. 'bar' looks like a pub but is a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotated means turned on an axis, so it went round.

clue.text: Special slant identifying clothing ornament

blocks.note: a slant or point of view

explanation.surface: A particular viewpoint picks out a decoration on a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A spangle is a small glittering disc sewn onto clothing as decoration, much like a sequin.

clue.text: A human made it: a truth Irish broadcasters accepted

indicators.note: the phrase accepted the broadcasters, taking them in

blocks.note: Raidió Teilifís Éireann, Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: Irish broadcasters concede that a human did it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A human made it' reads as a confession, but it is the definition; RTE, Ireland's state broadcaster, sits between the words for 'a truth'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object crafted by people, as opposed to a natural one.

clue.text: Scottish prosecutor, female, is about fifty

explanation.surface: A woman prosecutor in Scotland is around fifty years old.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the procurator fiscal, called the fiscal for short, is the public prosecutor.

clue.text: After fine, daughter leaves city — does a runner!

indicators.note: the daughter leaves the city, so that letter goes from its name

explanation.surface: After being fined, a daughter leaves the city and absconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After fine' puts F first; 'does a runner' is British slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a runner is British slang for running away, often to avoid paying, so it means flees.

clue.text: Daydreaming? Shearers may be doing it

blocks.note: second meaning, taken literally: collecting fleece from sheep

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for daydreaming comes from wandering about collecting tufts of wool snagged on hedges, which the second half takes at face value.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an idiom for idle reverie, and read literally it describes the farm task of gathering fleece.

clue.text: Sash former pupil originally introduced

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An old boy first brought in a sash.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash tied around a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Ultimately hostile in a sense, practising a form of discrimination

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of hostile is kept
in sets the kept letter inside the phrase for a sense

blocks.note: the gist is the general sense

explanation.surface: Someone is hostile in some sense, given to prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase, so the answer works as an adjective: an ageist attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An ageist discriminates against people because of their age, so the adjective describes practising that prejudice.

clue.text: Creator of placard nibbled by ruminants

indicators.note: a thing nibbled by animals is held in their mouths, so it goes inside

explanation.surface: Whoever made the poster sees it chewed by grazing animals.
explanation.walkthrough: DE(SIGN)ER. 'Creator of placard' reads as one phrase, but 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer is one who conceives and creates things, such as clothes or buildings.
